title: PyTorch Cheatsheet
name: PyTorch Cheatsheet
description: Fast reference for PyTorch syntax and common engineering lookups.
purpose: This cheatsheet is the fastest retrieval layer for PyTorch reference work, designed for rapid recall and navigation. It helps engineers find the right API area quickly, copy the relevant syntax from later modules, and move between the cheatsheet and the package page without reading long explanations. Use it when you already know the task and need the shortest path to the relevant PyTorch entry. It complements the PyTorch Package resource by staying lightweight and syntax-oriented, while the Package page owns fuller implementation knowledge and task guidance.
usage_guidelines: Start here when you need a quick PyTorch lookup rather than a conceptual explanation.
Use the section titles to jump directly to the functional area you need.
Search by API name first when you know the symbol you are looking for.
Search by task wording when you know the engineering goal but not the exact API.
Use the package page for broader implementation context, then return here for fast lookup.
Keep search terms short and specific to improve retrieval speed.
Prefer canonical PyTorch names and namespaces when searching.
Use this cheatsheet as a reference layer, not as a substitute for package-level guidance.
Follow links to the package resource when you need more context than syntax recall.
Treat this page as the entry point for fast navigation across PyTorch topics.

sections.title: Tensor Operations
sections.description: This section groups tensor creation, shape, indexing, and elementwise operation lookups. Use it when you need a tensor-level API or operator quickly.

sections.title: Autograd
sections.description: This section covers gradient-related lookup for automatic differentiation and gradient control. Use it when you are checking how to trace or manage gradients.

sections.title: Neural Network Modules
sections.description: This section organizes module-level building blocks for model definition and composition. Use it when you need to locate layer or module names quickly.

sections.title: Loss Functions
sections.description: This section groups objective-related entries for supervised and self-supervised training. Use it when you need to find a loss by task or training setup.

sections.title: Optimizers & LR Scheduling
sections.description: This section collects optimizer and scheduling references in one place. Use it when you are looking up parameter updates or learning-rate control.

sections.title: Data Loading
sections.description: This section covers dataset, sampler, and data pipeline lookups. Use it when you need to work with input pipelines or batching.

sections.title: Training Utilities
sections.description: This section collects training-loop support, state handling, and related helper lookups. Use it when you need utilities around model training workflows.

sections.title: Distributed & AMP
sections.description: This section groups distributed training and mixed-precision lookup together. Use it when scaling across devices or reducing numerical precision.

sections.title: Export & Deployment
sections.description: This section covers export and deployment-oriented lookup paths. Use it when you need a reference for moving models beyond training.

sections.title: TorchVision
sections.description: This section groups vision-oriented references related to PyTorch’s companion ecosystem. Use it when your lookup is centered on image workflows.

version_compatibility: This cheatsheet is aligned to the latest stable PyTorch 2.7.0 release and its documented support window for Python 3.10 through 3.14. It is intended for the PyTorch 2.x major line, with compatibility expectations centered on stable, documented APIs and release-note-driven changes. For PyTorch 2.x, expect the cheatsheet to remain usable across minor releases, but verify version-specific behavior when a lookup depends on a newly stabilized feature or a release-note change. The main modernization note for PyTorch 2.x is to prefer current documented interfaces and check the official docs or release notes before relying on older syntax patterns.
